history.period: Late 17th to early 19th century - second capital of the Kingdom of Sikkim, 1670-1814
history.summary: KEEP-OR-DROP FLAG: Rabdengtse is NOT a temple - it is the ruined former (second) capital of the Kingdom of Sikkim, now an Archaeological Survey of India-protected archaeological site (declared a monument of national importance). Recommend exclusion from the temples list or reclassification as a historic site. CSV TOWN NOTE: the CSV town 'Geyzing' is approximate - the ruins lie close to Pelling (a short drive plus a ~1-2 km forest walk), a few km from Gyalshing (Geyzing) town, in Gyalshing district. Established in 1670 by the second Chogyal Tensung Namgyal, son of the first Chogyal Phuntsog Namgyal, by shifting the capital from Yuksom (consecrated 1642). Rabdentse flourished for nearly 150 years as the seat of the Namgyal dynasty, with a grand palace complex of royal residence wings, courtyards, prayer chortens, a durbar area for public audiences, the Namphogang stone throne (three seats) where royal judges gave verdicts, and the Dab Lhagang royal prayer room; Pemayangtse Monastery stands close by. The capital was destroyed by the invading Gurkha army in 1814; the Chogyal then shifted the capital to Tumlong (1814-1894) and later Gangtok, as Rabdentse was considered too close to the Nepalese border. Today the palace foundations and chortens stand in a clearing with superb views of the Kanchenjunga range. Coordinates 27.30257, 88.25542 from map.geocode (matched 'Rabdentse Ruins, Gyalshing'), agreeing with Wikipedia (27.30111, 88.25389).

name: Rabdengtse Ruins
town_description: Pelling, at about 2,150 m in Gyalshing district of West Sikkim, is Sikkim's premier hill resort town with close views of Kanchenjunga. It lies about 130-145 km west of Gangtok (verify). Nearby attractions include Pemayangtse Monastery, Sanga Choeling Monastery, the Pelling Sky Walk with the Chenrezig statue, Khecheopalri Lake and Darap village; the Rabdentse ruins are a short drive plus a forest walk away.
tradition: Historic site (former royal capital) - not a temple
